NetMon Roots is developed with a lot of time, dedication, and the goal of providing Linux users with a powerful and secure tool free of charge.

Free software depends on support from its community. Every new feature, every bugfix, and every test across Linux distributions involves many hours of volunteer development work.

If you like NetMon Roots and want to support the project, a voluntary donation of 5 € or more is appreciated.

Your support helps to

- develop new features,
- fix bugs,
- test NetMon on more Linux distributions,
- operate the website and infrastructure, and
- keep the project free for all Linux users in the long term.

Every contribution - regardless of amount - helps keep free software alive.

Thank you for your support and your trust in NetMon Roots!

tour_full_step_intro_body: This guided run goes through the areas collected in the tour tab one by one. It is much more detailed than the quick start and is suitable for a complete walkthrough.
tour_full_step_done_body: You have now gone through all currently covered tour areas in sequence. For individual topics you can later jump back into the specialized or tab tours.

tour_dns_intro_body: This tour shows you the most important DNS functions: selection, apply, DNS Guard and DNS over TLS.
tour_dns_done_body: For a practical start, choose a DNS profile now, apply it and then observe DNS Guard and DoT.
tour_quickstart_intro_body: This guided overview shows you the structure of NetMon: main areas, subtabs, side modules, security, analysis, support and the main entry points.
tour_quickstart_status_body: Here you see the compact live status for Internet, VPN, firewall, killswitch, IP and stealth mode. The header is the fastest place for a daily overview.
tour_quickstart_status_hint: If something turns red or yellow here, it is usually worth checking DNS, Security or the log first.
tour_quickstart_system_actions_body: Use this button to run central system actions only after a security confirmation. This is the operational entry point for quick administration tasks.
tour_quickstart_system_actions_hint: System actions are intentionally centralized and not scattered across the whole interface.
tour_quickstart_quickslots_body: This area contains link slots and VPN slots for recurring targets and profiles. It is designed for quick access in everyday use.
tour_quickstart_quickslots_hint: If you use NetMon regularly, this saves many manual steps.
tour_quickstart_side_modules_body: The wide right area is intended for structured companion modules such as the security system check. It complements the main tabs without overloading the core area.
tour_quickstart_side_modules_hint: Many check and collection views are intentionally moved here so the main workflow stays clear.
tour_quickstart_radio_quick_body: Media functions remain directly reachable without interrupting the main workflow in the tabs.
tour_quickstart_radio_quick_hint: The quick access is intentionally compact and points you to the radio tab for depth.
tour_quickstart_system_main_body: The system main area bundles local states, drives, links and system-related management blocks. This is where daily system work usually starts.
tour_quickstart_system_main_hint: The subtabs in the system area keep monitoring, drives and slot logic clearly separated.
tour_quickstart_system_monitor_body: This subtab shows utilization, hardware, uptime and basic system data. It is the technical starting point for performance and state questions.
tour_quickstart_system_monitor_hint: If NetMon feels sluggish or the system looks suspicious, this is usually the first checkpoint.
tour_quickstart_hdd_body: Here you manage drive slots, mount states and various storage functions. This area is designed for controlled device work instead of ad-hoc shell steps.
tour_quickstart_hdd_hint: Especially useful if you work with multiple drives or LUKS/mount workflows.
tour_quickstart_links_body: The links subtab complements the quick slots and serves as an organized target board for frequently used programs, destinations or work paths.
tour_quickstart_links_hint: Designed for recurring paths instead of one-off ad-hoc actions.
tour_quickstart_tools_main_body: The tools area contains diagnostic, analysis, convenience and experimental functions. This is NetMon's toolbox.
tour_quickstart_tools_main_hint: Everything that checks, helps, visualizes or adds extra value ends up here.
tour_quickstart_mtr_body: The MTR subtab combines packet timings and hop visibility in a running target analysis. It is useful for network paths that behave unstably over time.
tour_quickstart_mtr_hint: Good for routes that are not permanently broken but only become bad at times.
tour_quickstart_nmap_body: This area contains port scanning and target checks with prepared profiles. It is meant for structured target analysis, not uncontrolled poking around.
tour_quickstart_nmap_hint: Useful for visibility, services and first fingerprints of a system.
tour_quickstart_iftop_body: The iftop subtab watches live traffic by source and destination. Here you can quickly see which connections are consuming bandwidth.
tour_quickstart_iftop_hint: Practical for load spikes or when network traffic suddenly looks unusual.
tour_quickstart_htop_body: Here you get a compact view of processes, CPU load and runtime behavior. This area complements the system monitor with a process-oriented perspective.
tour_quickstart_htop_hint: Helpful when you want to map system load to a process view instead of just seeing the load.
tour_quickstart_theme_studio_body: In Theme Studio you adjust NetMon's look, colors and visual profiles. This area belongs to UI maintenance, not security or network operations.
tour_quickstart_theme_studio_hint: Intentionally separated from operational functions so design and technical work do not get mixed.
tour_quickstart_trace_body: The trace area is used for path and hop analysis of network targets. It helps narrow down routing or reachability problems.
tour_quickstart_trace_hint: A good fit when DNS already resolves but the target still behaves strangely.
tour_quickstart_connections_body: Here you see active network connections together with their processes. This is the right area when you want to know who is talking to whom.
tour_quickstart_connections_hint: Helpful for unknown connections, leak questions or mapping a connection back to a process.
tour_quickstart_dns_body: In the DNS tab you control resolvers, DNS Guard, DNSSEC and DoT. With this button you apply the current DNS selection.
tour_quickstart_dns_hint: The DNS tab is opened automatically for this step.
tour_quickstart_dns_action_failure: DNS profile manager could not be opened.
tour_quickstart_chad_analysis_body: Prepared analyses and merged findings come together here. This area is meant to turn technical results into understandable follow-up analysis.
tour_quickstart_chad_analysis_hint: Useful when several findings from different tabs should be brought into a shared context.
tour_quickstart_chad_settings_body: Here you configure the analysis assistant's model, behavior, focus and filter logic. This area therefore controls the analysis process more than the system state.
tour_quickstart_chad_settings_hint: Important if answers should become shorter, more technical or more risk-oriented.
tour_quickstart_security_block_title: Security as its own main block
tour_quickstart_security_block_body: In NetMon, Security is its own workspace for protection, checks and traceable diagnostic paths.
tour_quickstart_radio_body: The radio area provides station control, EQ, a miniplayer and optionally detached operation.
tour_quickstart_radio_hint: The tools area with radio is opened for this step.
tour_quickstart_radio_action_failure: Radio tab could not be opened.
tour_quickstart_fun_body: This area intentionally does not belong to the core operation, but it is part of the lab. Extra functions and playful components live here.
tour_quickstart_fun_hint: Intentionally separated from the productive core so structure and focus stay intact.
tour_quickstart_linux_help_body: Here NetMon bundles hints about Linux commands, workflows and typical system paths. The tab is intended as a reference and learning area.
tour_quickstart_linux_help_hint: Practical when you want to move directly from a finding into a Linux work path.
tour_quickstart_cleanup_body: This area is reserved for guided cleanup and maintenance workflows. It is meant to encourage structured steps instead of uncontrolled deletion actions.
tour_quickstart_cleanup_hint: Important for later safe cleanup flows with context and safety markers.
tour_quickstart_security_main_body: This is where Security Monitoring, firewall, guards, process observation, ClamAV, audits and packet capture live. It is NetMon's central protection and checking area.
tour_quickstart_security_main_hint: The matching Security subtab is prepared automatically.
tour_quickstart_firewall_body: Here you control UFW, logging, listeners and security-relevant network states. The tab connects active rules with observable network facts.
tour_quickstart_firewall_hint: A core area for allow rules, blocks and port visibility.
tour_quickstart_guards_body: This is where Device Guard, input access and other local protection views live. This area looks more at changes and trust boundaries than at classic network data.
tour_quickstart_guards_hint: Relevant when local devices, input access or baselines look suspicious.
tour_quickstart_path_guard_body: PATH Guard checks PATH entries and shell profiles for suspicious search paths, ordering and manipulation.
tour_quickstart_path_guard_hint: Especially useful when shell profiles or user-bin paths look suspicious.
tour_quickstart_process_guard_body: Process Guard highlights suspicious processes, start chains, paths and execution patterns. It is one of the most important areas for suspicious behavior.
tour_quickstart_process_guard_hint: Especially strong when you want to understand process findings rather than only see them.
tour_quickstart_clamav_body: This is where local virus scans, signature state, quarantine and classic file checks come together. The area complements D-Scan with traditional scanning work.
tour_quickstart_clamav_hint: Good for systematic checks of folders, files and findings.
tour_quickstart_lynis_body: Lynis checks hardening, configuration and the overall security state of the system. The focus is on audit and recommendations rather than live events.
tour_quickstart_lynis_hint: Useful for general security assessments and hardening guidance.
tour_quickstart_rkhunter_body: rkhunter covers rootkit and integrity questions. Here you check deeper manipulation suspicions rather than everyday operational anomalies.
tour_quickstart_rkhunter_hint: More suitable for focused security checks than for everyday viewing.
tour_quickstart_repository_guard_body: This area is intended for package sources, signatures and security-relevant source changes. It belongs to the system's extended chain of trust.
tour_quickstart_repository_guard_hint: Structurally important even if the practical implementation can still grow.
tour_quickstart_roots_baseline_body: Here you watch sensitive root and baseline areas for changes. The focus is on critical filesystem states and deviations.
tour_quickstart_roots_baseline_hint: Relevant when critical paths or baselines change unexpectedly.
tour_quickstart_startup_guard_body: Startup Guard monitors autostart, systemd and persistence paths. This lets you detect new start mechanisms or unexpected boot/login entries.
tour_quickstart_startup_guard_hint: One of the most important areas for persistence and unwanted autostarts.
tour_quickstart_packet_capture_body: In the packet capture tab you start captures and prepare raw network data for analysis or export.

tour_quickstart_log_hint: Many questions are answered faster through the log than through guesswork.

tour_tab_desc_secure_browser: Secure Browser creates separate, hardened Firefox instances with their own profile for selected websites. Cookies, website storage, history, logins and settings therefore stay isolated instead of merging into one shared online identity in your everyday browser.
tour_tab_hint_secure_browser: The largest benefit comes from opening each sensitive or heavily tracked web application exclusively in its own instance.
tour_tab_secure_browser_gain_body: The installation creates a technical boundary between web services. A bank, mail account, social network or another sensitive site receives its own browser state. Trackers and embedded content cannot simply access the cookie, login and storage state of your everyday browser or another Secure Browser instance. This primarily reduces cross-service correlation and accidental mixing of identities.
tour_tab_secure_browser_hardening_body: The generated instance can disable telemetry, Studies, Pocket, Sync, WebRTC, form and search suggestions, and speculative network requests. Strict content and tracking protection, HTTPS-Only and blocked third-party cookies reduce additional data exposure. Security profiles let you make a deliberate tradeoff between compatibility and strict separation.
tour_tab_secure_browser_filter_title: Website filter as a narrow trust boundary
tour_tab_secure_browser_filter_body: With the website filter enabled, the default is to block and only configured domains are allowed. This makes accidental browsing, unrelated login flows and unexpected redirects harder. Required authentication, payment or CDN domains must be added deliberately; an overly broad allowlist weakens the benefit.
tour_tab_secure_browser_persistence_titl: Choose cookie and login persistence deliberately
tour_tab_secure_browser_persistence_body: When cookies are not retained, the instance removes sessions, history, cache and other local traces more consistently on exit. Persistent cookies improve convenience but also preserve recognizable identifiers. A dedicated persistent login can be useful for banking or mail; an ephemeral state provides more privacy for infrequent or particularly sensitive use.
tour_tab_secure_browser_dry_run_body: Dry Run shows the profile, allowed domains, policies and planned files before creating the browser instance. Review domain exceptions, cookie behavior, password manager and security profile in particular. Only then should Create install the prepared configuration.
tour_tab_secure_browser_limits_body: Secure Browser improves separation and data minimization, but it does not make you anonymous. Websites still see your public IP, can evaluate browser and device characteristics, and recognize you after you sign in to an account. A VPN or Tor is a separate protection layer; current browser versions, cautious permissions and a maintained allowlist remain necessary as well.

tooltips_by_source.System: Zentrale Systemübersicht von Net: System: central overview of NetMon's local system state. Use this tab to control and inspect operating state, important device blocks, storage, links and slot-related functions. It is mainly intended for day-to-day system work and a fast overview.
tooltips_by_source.Tools: Werkzeugbereich mit Netzwerk-, An: Tools: workspace for networking, analysis and helper functions. Here you find practical single-purpose tools such as MTR, Nmap, iftop, htop, Theme Studio, Radio and other project-related extras. This tab groups everything mainly used for support, inspection or experimentation.
tooltips_by_source.Security: Sicherheits- und Guard-Bereich: Security: NetMon's security and guard area. This is where firewall, guards, process monitoring, virus scanning, audits and capture functions come together. The tab is meant to keep protections, anomalies and security-relevant checks in one place.
tooltips_by_source.Log: Laufende Meldungen, Statusausgaben: Log: ongoing messages, status output and feedback from the application. Here you can track what NetMon is doing, which action ran last, and which results or errors occurred.
tooltips_by_source.Trace: Bereich für Netzwerktraces und Pf: Trace: area for network traces and path analysis. Use it to inspect routes, hops, latency and reachability when you want to understand network paths better or narrow down problems.
tooltips_by_source.Verbindungen: Übersicht und Analyse akti: Connections: overview and analysis of active network connections together with the involved processes. This tab helps you see who is connected to what and which processes are behind a connection.
tooltips_by_source.DNS: Bereich für Namensauflösung, DoT- u: DNS: area for name resolution, DoT and DNS-related checks. Here you configure, test and evaluate DNS behavior, protection features and possible leak situations.
tooltips_by_source.Chad: Analyse- und Assistenzbereich für: Chad: analysis and assistant area for prepared evaluations. Findings from other tabs land here so you can summarize, assess or analyze them further more quickly.
tooltips_by_source.Chad Einstellungen: Konfigurationsbereic: Chad Settings: configuration area for models, access and assistant behavior. Here you define how Chad works and which options are used in the analysis flow.
tooltips_by_source.Download Scan: Prüfbereich für Downloads: Download Scan: inspection area for downloads and single files. This tab helps you assess suspicious content before opening, launching or sharing it.
tooltips_by_source.Einstellungen: Allgemeine Konfiguration: Settings: general NetMon configuration. Here you control behavior, appearance, convenience features and various application options for daily use.
tooltips_by_source.System: Hauptansicht für den laufenden Z: System: main view for the current system state. It contains the central switches, status fields and core functions for local operation.
tooltips_by_source.HDD: Bereich für Speichergeräte, Mounts,: HDD: area for storage devices, mounts, encryption and related actions. Here you manage and inspect drives and their current state.
tooltips_by_source.Links: Sammlung für System- und Projektl: Links: collection of system and project links. This tab is a quick-access area for frequently used destinations and references.
tooltips_by_source.VPN Slots: Verwaltung mehrerer VPN-Profi: VPN Slots: management of multiple VPN profiles and slot assignments. Here you switch between configurations and keep an eye on the profile structure.
tooltips_by_source.MTR: Kombiniert Ping und Traceroute für: MTR: combines ping and traceroute for fast path and latency analysis. Useful when you want to make connection problems, hops or delays visible.
Nmap: area for host and port analysis. Here you check reachability, open services and common network questions around hosts and ports.
tooltips_by_source.iftop: Live-Blick auf aktuelle Netzwerkf: iftop: live view of current network flows and bandwidth usage. This tab helps you make active traffic visible quickly.
tooltips_by_source.htop: Schneller Überblick über Prozesse,: htop: quick overview of processes, CPU load and memory usage. Here you watch current system load directly and compactly.
tooltips_by_source.Theme Studio: Bereich zum Anpassen und P: Theme Studio: area for adjusting and reviewing NetMon's appearance. Here you change colors, visual style and interface details.
tooltips_by_source.Radio: Integrierter Audio- und Radiobere: Radio: integrated audio and radio area with station management and playback controls. This tab bundles NetMon's media functions.
tooltips_by_source.Fun: Bereich für projektnahe Extras und: Fun: area for project-related extras and playful add-ons. This is where things live that are not part of core operation but are intentionally part of the lab.
tooltips_by_source.Linux: Hilfen, Hinweise und Unterstützun: Linux: help, hints and support for Linux commands and typical workflows. Useful when you want to look up commands or support small Linux workflows directly inside the lab.
tooltips_by_source.Cleanup Assistant: Vorbereiteter Pflegeb: Cleanup Assistant: prepared maintenance area for analysis and safe cleanup steps. This is where cache, temp, log and trash checks are meant to run later in a guided flow with safety markings and confirmation.
tooltips_by_source.Firewall: Zentrale UFW-Ansicht von NetMo: Firewall: NetMon's central UFW view. Here you manage firewall status, rules, logging and quick UFW actions. You also see open listeners, port reality checks and direct hints about block events, suspected port scans, suspicious source IPs and frequent target ports.
tooltips_by_source.Guards: Sammelbereich für Device Guard u: Guards: combined area for Device Guard and PATH Guard. This tab helps you make local changes visible: connected input devices, current input access, baselines and PATH-related anomalies. It is especially useful when you want to understand which devices are present, who accesses them and whether local protection paths changed.
tooltips_by_source.Process Guard: Beobachtet laufende Proze: Process Guard: watches running processes and highlights suspicious launches, unusual paths, shell chains and unexpected executions. This is the core area for process findings, filters, trust lists, short assessments and deeper analysis of suspicious processes.
tooltips_by_source.ClamAV: Bereich für lokale Virenscans mi: ClamAV: area for local virus scans with ClamAV. Here you inspect signature state, scan status, findings, quarantine and typical quick or folder scans. The tab is suitable for classic file scans and tracking detected findings.
tooltips_by_source.Lynis: Audit- und Härtungsbereich für da: Lynis: audit and hardening area for the local system. Here you start security checks, review recommendations and assess configuration or hardening hints. Useful for a structured check of the system's overall security state.
tooltips_by_source.rkhunter: Rootkit- und Integritätsprüfun: rkhunter: rootkit and integrity checking for the system. Here you control rkhunter updates, scans and evaluation and get status, summaries and hints about possible tampering or suspicious system deviations.
tooltips_by_source.Repository Guard: Vorbereiteter Platzhal: Repository Guard: prepared placeholder for later monitoring of package sources, repository changes, signatures and security-relevant update sources. At the moment the tab only shows status, description, planned checkpoints and a disabled scan entry point.
tooltips_by_source.Roots Baseline Guard: Überwacht sensible: Roots Baseline Guard: monitors sensitive root and baseline areas for changes. Here you can spot new, changed or excluded entries and better assess whether critical system paths changed unexpectedly.
tooltips_by_source.Startup Guard: Prüft Autostart-, systemd: Startup Guard: checks autostart, systemd and other startup paths for new or changed entries. The tab is there to make unwanted persistence, new startup mechanisms or unusual changes in boot and login paths visible.
tooltips_by_source.Capture: Paketmitschnitt und lokale Netz: Capture: packet capture and local network analysis. Here you start recordings, inspect interfaces and collect raw data for troubleshooting, connection analysis or later evaluation in Wireshark.
